claims.scope: For k>=2 distinct prime divisors a_i of an odd n, canonical parabolics Sz(2^(n/a_i)) form a thick, residually connected, flag-transitive geometry. It is RWPRI if and only if e=n/product(a_i)>1.
claims.canonical_rank_range: 2<=k<=min(omega(n),Omega(n)-1), where omega counts distinct primes and Omega counts multiplicity
claims.not_claimed: Arbitrary relative positions sharing only maximal-parabolic isomorphism types

claims.scope: Every literal Construction11 parameter admits canonical simultaneous realization, exact field intersections, RWPRI, geometry, thickness, residual connectedness and flag transitivity.
claims.reading_depth: Primary definitions and construction statement read; independent page-image audit

claims.scope: The rank-four all-simple family at n=3^2*5*7*11=3465 satisfies F/RC/FT/RWPRI but is absent from the eleven literal constructions. Construction11 caps rank at m-1=3 and Constructions1-10 contain soluble parabolics.
claims.qualification: This is an omission from the literal exhaustive list for the stated subgroup systems. Adding suitable truncations or correcting the Construction11 bound would include it; no claim that natural extensions of the constructions cannot produce it.

claims.scope: Every embedded Q=(E_q nonsplit-extension E_t):C_(t-1), for t=2^e with odd e>1 dividing the odd exponent of q, is conjugate to Z_q U_t H_t.

For a proper H<=Z_q U_t H_t with full odd part t-1 and a non-elementary normal Sylow-2 subgroup, H maps onto Q/Z_q. Its overgroups correspond exactly to F_t-subspaces of F_q containing H intersect Z_q; maximality is equivalent to center quotient dimension one.

Every intended Construction10 lattice has canonical bare embeddings. No embedding with its prescribed mixed parabolic and pairwise mixed intersection types is RWPRI, because all remaining intersections are nonmaximal at the mixed-parabolic residue.
claims.RWPRI: impossible for every admissible parameter of the intended lattice
not_claimed: Failure of geometry or flag transitivity
Exclusion of arbitrary systems with the same parabolic types but different intersections
